key_insight: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT) treats attention keys and values as reusable memory across depths and loops. This lets repeated Transformer computations selectively access earlier information rather than relying only on the connection between adjacent loops.
problem_solved: Looped Transformers increase expressivity by repeatedly applying shared layers, but this adds computational cost. The paper explores what information should pass between loops to improve the expressivity–efficiency trade-off.
method: Reuse shared Transformer layers across multiple loops.
Introduce Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA), which uses keys and values as memory for selective reuse across depths and loops.
Include a loop-residual variant, MoLT-R, that retains the residual stream; further details are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: MoLT offers a design direction for making repeated Transformer computation more useful through selective memory reuse. The supplied abstract does not include results, so efficiency gains and practical benefits cannot be quantified.
visual_elements: An unrolled loop diagram showing the same Transformer layers reused across iterations.
A key–value memory bank with selective connections to attention at different depths and loops.

paper_authors: Lianghui Zhu, Shijie Wang, Xinggang Wang, Jinze Bai, Bo Wang
